Thm. 2.12.

Countable union of countable sets is countable.

Proof

Enumerate the elements diagonally, e.g. x11,x12,x13,…x_{11},x_{12},x_{13},\ldotsx11​,x12​,x13​,…, x21,x22,x23,…x_{21},x_{22},x_{23},\ldotsx21​,x22​,x23​,…, …

Thm. 2.13.

Set of finite tuples whose elements are in a countable set is countable: (a1,…,an)(a_1,\ldots,a_n)(a1​,…,an​).

Proof

Induction. Let BnB_nBn​ be the set of n-tuples. The (n+1)(n+1)(n+1)-tuples are obtained from Bn×B1B_n\times B_1Bn​×B1​; apply Thm. 2.12.

Cor.

The set of all rational numbers is countable.
